html:
The siege of Dorostolon, modern Silistra on the lower Danube, was fought in 971 between the Byzantine Empire under John I Tzimiskes and the Rus' of Prince Sviatoslav I of Kiev.

Byzantium had first paid Sviatoslav to attack the Bulgarians. But he conquered much of Bulgaria for himself, planned to move his capital to the Danube, and threatened Constantinople. In spring 971 Tzimiskes struck, took the Bulgarian capital Preslav and shut Sviatoslav up in Dorostolon. For three months the Rus' made fierce sallies, but the Byzantines held the river with fire-throwing ships and the land with their heavy cavalry.

In July Sviatoslav made peace. He gave up Bulgaria and swore not to attack the empire again, in return for safe passage home and food for his men. On the way back to Kiev he was ambushed and killed by the Pechenegs in 972. Eastern Bulgaria came under direct Byzantine rule, though the west soon rose under Tsar Samuel.
